title: Night-time in Paranal
caption: The Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds over the Auxiliary Telescopes, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way is clearly visible above three of the four VLT Auxiliary Telescopes in this view of the sky over Paranal, home of ESO's Very Large Telescope. On the left side of the image are the Large Magellanic Cloud, lower down, and the Small Magellanic Cloud, above it.

The Auxiliary Telescopes are 1.8 meters across and are used only for interferometry. By combining their light, this technique lets astronomers see details up to 25 times finer than a single telescope could show. Their arrangement can be changed by moving them between 30 different observing positions on the platform.
The Magellanic Clouds are nearby irregular dwarf galaxies. From the southern hemisphere they are easy to see with the unaided eye.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The Magellanic Clouds are visible to the unaided eye from the south, but a long camera exposure gathers more light and shows them and the Milky Way in greater detail.

explore: The photograph was taken by ESO Photo Ambassador Christoph Malin, who captured three of the Auxiliary Telescopes against the sky over Paranal, with two neighboring galaxies in the same frame.
alt: Three telescopes under the Milky Way, with two fuzzy dwarf galaxies on the left side of the sky.
